prerequisites: Foundations from mechanics and mathematics, thermodynamics, electrical engineering, mechanical and drive technology, and fluid mechanics
Positive completion of the StEOP (StudienEingangs- und OrientierungsPhase)

learning_outcomes.text: The introductory module for the specialization Vehicles and Mobility provides fundamental knowledge of the basics of vehicle dynamics for road vehicles, rail vehicles, water vehicles, and aircraft (with a focus on the first two types), and gives a systematic overview of current and future vehicle propulsion systems and the relevant technical principles. In the 'Fundamentals of Vehicle Dynamics' lecture, students learn essential aspects of modeling in vehicle dynamics, and can specify suitable, simple vehicle models for selected questions and formulate the corresponding equations of motion and model laws. Based on these system equations, essential dynamic phenomena of longitudinal, lateral, and vertical dynamics are discussed, and the influence of essential design parameters is analyzed. In the 'Sustainable Mobility' lecture, the structure, function, and interrelationships of the main propulsion systems - internal combustion engine, hybrid drives, battery-electric and fuel cell-electric propulsion systems - are explained and supplemented by central aspects such as energy management and environmental impact. Development processes/market trends are analyzed against the background of legal frameworks. A central cross-cutting theme is ecological assessment using life cycle analyses, including energy and fuel provision.
reproduce simple vehicle models and the associated system equations and model limits.
analyze and interpret these system equations with regard to fundamental problems in vehicle dynamics.
derive and discuss the forces and moments determining the vehicle system behavior.
discuss investigations of critical driving conditions and questions of stability, and present the influence of essential parameters.

systematically understand future vehicle propulsion systems (internal combustion engine, hybrid, battery-electric, and fuel cell-based drives) and technically correctly explain their technical principles, structure, and function.
comprehend, grasp, and comparatively present interrelationships, energy flows, and fundamental aspects of energy management in different propulsion systems.
objectively analyze environmental impacts of vehicle propulsion systems, especially emissions and energy consumption, based on fundamental assessment approaches.
critically classify and analyze development processes and market trends in sustainable mobility, considering legal and regulatory frameworks.
comprehend, interpret, and argumentatively discuss ecological assessments of vehicle propulsion systems using life cycle analyses (LCA) including energy and fuel provision.
structure and summarize fundamentals, methods, and results, and present them in writing.
formulate lines of argument for questions clearly, comprehensibly, and precisely.
objectively reflect on and reasonably evaluate sustainability-related decisions and conflicts of objectives in the context of technical developments, considering cost-benefit trade-offs.

syllabus_topics: Fundamentals of vehicle dynamics for land, water, and air vehicles, with a focus on road and rail vehicles
Basic vehicle models, system equations for description, analysis, and interpretation of longitudinal, lateral, and vertical vehicle dynamics

Fundamentals for understanding driving behavior, lane keeping, driving stability, braking behavior, propulsion, driving comfort, tire-road and wheel-rail contact, model laws of water vehicles, characteristic driving and flight conditions
Overview of current and future vehicle propulsion systems
Internal combustion engine, hybrid, battery-electric, and fuel cell-electric propulsion systems
Structure and function of propulsion systems

assessment_methods.method: Written and/or oral examination on theoretical fundamentals

assessment_rules: Written and/or oral examination on the theoretical fundamentals. The applied teaching and learning methods, as well as the examination modalities, are to be specified in the information system for studies and teaching before the start of each semester.
